discussion_comments.comment_body: Fair catch. Before this PR a `metadata: null` clear was encoded as `{}` and the daemon wiped the record; my rewrite sent a literal `null`, which `asPlainRecord` decodes as omitted, so the clear became a no-op. No desktop or CLI caller passes `metadata: null` over the hub today, but it was a semantic change this diff introduced, so restored the `{}` encoding in 3e428e6dc and added a test for it.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Added in 3fe2f2a: `sqlite-cron-store.bun-test.ts` runs under `bun test` (the Desktop runtime, bun:sqlite) and (1) asserts bun:sqlite binds named parameters by exact token — unprefixed keys bind NULL, prefixed keys bind the value; (2) end-to-end: claimDueRuns claims a due one-off run (status=running). It is wired into @cline/core test:unit so CI runs it after vitest. Verified locally: bun 2/2 pass, vitest 19/19 pass, typecheck clean.

In general, it is better if we can reflect the "only set for `beforeRun`" in a TypeScript shape which has `{foo: "beforeRun", entry: "run" | "continue", ...}` so the rest of the system can use these fields in a typesafe way. Also possible to lift a property out of an object by construction to relate these fields with some other state. (Does that make sense? TL;DR, can we use the type system here to communicate "only set for `beforeRun`" and benefit from checking?)
